package_info.package_manager: n/a (malware binary, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: 8base is a ransomware family that encrypts and exfiltrates user files, demands ransom for decryption, and threatens to leak stolen data. It kills processes to maximize file encryption, selectively targets files/folders, and uses anti-forensics techniques. It is delivered via malware loaders such as SmokeLoader and is designed for financial extortion.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if filename contains any of ['ntldr', 'ntdetect.com', 'io.sys', 'recov']: skip file; if file is in ['C:\Windows', 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Caches']: skip file;
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks file and folder names to avoid encrypting critical system files and certain directories, ensuring system stability and maximizing impact on user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Selective targeting of files and folders is a common ransomware evasion and persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not avoid encrypting or modifying only user data while skipping system files for extortion purposes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or migration tools may skip system files to avoid corruption, but not for malicious encryption.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates and terminates a list of processes (databases, office apps, mail clients) to ensure files are not locked and can be encrypted.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Killing a wide range of user and business application processes is a hallmark of ransomware, aiming to maximize file encryption coverage.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not indiscriminately kill unrelated processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System maintenance tools may close processes for updates, but not for mass file encryption.
key_indicators: Bulk process termination targeting productivity and database apps

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if file.size < 1.5MB: encrypt entire file; else: inject 0x40000 null bytes at intervals, encrypt last 0xC0000 bytes, add encrypted metadata;
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code determines file size and applies full or partial encryption, injecting null bytes and encrypting file tails to speed up the process and hinder recovery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Partial encryption and data injection are advanced ransomware techniques to increase speed and complicate recovery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not partially encrypt or corrupt files in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only ransomware uses this pattern.
key_indicators: Conditional full/partial encryption based on file size
Null byte injection and metadata tampering

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encryption, the code renames each file to include a unique victim ID and attacker contact email, signaling compromise and facilitating ransom negotiation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending attacker-controlled extensions is a clear ransomware indicator.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not rename files to include attacker contact information.
key_indicators: File extension includes attacker email and unique ID

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: write ransom note to info.hta and info.txt in affected directories
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encryption, the code drops ransom notes in multiple formats to inform the victim and provide payment instructions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping ransom notes is a universal ransomware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not demand payment for file recovery.
key_indicators: Creation of ransom notes in affected directories

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: exfiltrate stolen files to file sharing services (Gofile, Pixeldrain, files.dp.ua, AnonFiles, Anonym File, Mega)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encryption, the code uploads stolen files to public file sharing services, enabling data leak extortion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of sensitive files to attacker-controlled infrastructure is a critical data breach indicator.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not exfiltrate user data to public file sharing services.
key_indicators: Network connections to file sharing services

attack_chain.action: Initial infection via SmokeLoader or other loader
Ransomware process starts, scans for files and folders to target/exclude
Kills processes to unlock files for encryption
Encrypts files (full or partial based on size), injects null bytes, adds metadata
Renames encrypted files to include victim ID and attacker email
Drops ransom notes in affected directories
Exfiltrates stolen files to public file sharing services

behavioral_signatures: Bulk process termination targeting productivity/database applications
Selective file/folder exclusion during mass file operations
Conditional full/partial file encryption with null byte injection
File renaming to include attacker email and unique ID
Creation of ransom notes (.hta/.txt) in user directories
Network connections to public file sharing services post-encryption
file_indicators: Presence of info.hta and info.txt ransom notes
Exclusion of files/folders: ntldr, ntdetect.com, io.sys, recov, C:\Windows, C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Caches
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Gofile, Pixeldrain, files.dp.ua, AnonFiles, Anonym File, Mega
Potential C2 or exfiltration traffic after file encryption
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for bulk process termination events, especially targeting office/database applications, and for mass file renaming with attacker email patterns. Detect creation of ransom notes (.hta/.txt) in user directories. Watch for outbound connections to known file sharing services following suspicious file operations. Alert on files with .8base extensions and unique victim IDs. Correlate these behaviors for high-confidence ransomware detection.
